title: Inhaled sedation in the critically ill patient
official: Inhaled sedation in the critically ill patient: a multicentre randomised clinical trial
summary: Main objective: To compare the days free of mechanical ventilation in patients receiving sedation with isoflurane versus those receiving intravenous sedation with propofol in critically ill patients in whom more than 48 hours of invasive mechanical ventilation are expected.

interventions.name: Sedaconda 100% líquido para inhalación del vapor
Propofol Fresenius 20 mg/ml emulsión para inyección o perfusión

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age equal to or greater than 18 years
2. Mechanically ventilated patients in whom a minimum mechanical ventilation time of 48 hours from randomization is expected.
3. Patients in whom it is necessary to maintain a RASS between -3 and -5.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Contraindication for isoflurane or propofol.
2. Acute neurological pathology (head trauma, intraparenchymal hemorrhage, subarachnoid hemorrhage or post-operative neurosurgery).
3. Any type of disorder (blindness, deafness, dementia) or language barrier that prevents the completion of the scales for the assessment of delirium or cognitive assessment.
4. Life expectancy of less than 48 hours or patients with such a level of severity that death during admission to the ICU is considered highly probable.
5. Patients in whom repeated surgical interventions are expected during their stay in the ICU.
6. Patients with extracorporeal oxygenation system (ECMO).
7. Mandatory need for active humidification.
8. Need for benzodiazepine use due to a specific indication (e.g., withdrawal syndrome).
9. Neuromuscular disease or high spinal cord injury that may prevent weaning from mechanical ventilation due to baseline condition.
10. Lack of informed consent.
11. Patients with extracorporeal CO2 extraction system (ECCO2R).
12. Critical burn patients.
13. Patients admitted due to recovered cardiorespiratory arrest.
14. History of ventricular tachycardia/long QT syndrome.
15. Patients who have remained on mechanical ventilation for more than 48 hours at the time of randomization.
16. Tidal volume less than 300 ml or PaCO2 greater than 50 mm Hg at the time of randomization.
17. Pregnancy.
18. History of allergy or intolerance to isoflurane.
